title: Gerund or Infinitive? The Complete Masterlist for Error Spotting in Bank PO
excerpt: Why do we say 'look forward to meeting you' and not 'look forward to meet you'? Master the 25 fixed expressions that require a gerund after 'to'.
content:
In standard English grammar, the preposition 'to' is usually followed by a bare verb (Infinitive: to go, to eat, to learn). But in specific idiomatic phrases, 'to' acts as a standard preposition and must be followed by a noun or Gerund (V-ing).

The High-Yield 'Prepositional TO' List

Memorize these 8 high-frequency exam phrases that MUST take a Gerund:

  • Look forward to + V-ing (I look forward to hearing from you.)
  • With a view to + V-ing (He joined the coaching with a view to improving his score.)
  • Used to / Accustomed to + V-ing (She is used to studying late at night.)
  • Given to / Devoted to + V-ing
  • Object to / Averse to + V-ing
  • Prone to + V-ing
